A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RECON with the same authors, core method and experimental domains. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete Appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original symmetry-recovery, OOD-detection and classification results on MNIST, FashionMNIST and GEOM-QM9, plus centroid simulations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds evaluated comparators, neighborhood diagnostics, failure cases and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the class-pose backbones, Fréchet normalization, learned mappings Θ and Λ, losses and inference formulas remain unchanged. The Tukey-Fréchet extension already appears in v2. The revised image neighborhood size is a hyperparameter change, not a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use MNIST, FashionMNIST and GEOM-QM9 for pose recovery, OOD detection and classification under rotations, alongside the same synthetic SO(2) centroid simulations. Added comparisons and diagnostics remain within this existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds EquiAdapt to the frozen-classifier canonicalization comparisons on all three datasets in Figure 6d. New Table 3 evaluates ESCNN and Partial G-CNN classifiers on the images and a SEGNN classifier on GEOM-QM9. The existing IE-AE comparisons and qualitative SGM comparison are retained.

E3.justification: The reported image pseudo-label neighborhood changes from k=25 to k=10, while GEOM-QM9 retains k=25. v3 also introduces comparator-training protocols, hyperparameter sweeps, and selection of the worst 5,000 FashionMNIST inputs for failure analysis. Appendix F explicitly selects EquiAdapt and ESCNN hyperparameters by test accuracy; existing RECON training budgets and data splits largely remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2's neighborhood-size and molecular hit-rate analyses are substantially extended. v3 adds FashionMNIST and GEOM-QM9 neighborhood sensitivity, worst-molecule error, image hit rates, a FashionMNIST neighbor-confusion matrix and low-hit-rate examples. Appendix D.5 adds computational-cost and inference-overhead analyses.

E5.justification: Although v2 already displays some dispersion, v3 adds ± reporting to OOD scores, downstream accuracies and reference accuracies in Figures 5c–6d and Table 2. Figure 10 explicitly identifies image sensitivity bands as standard deviations across runs with different seeds. Run counts and the meaning of all tabulated ± terms remain unspecified.

E6.justification: Figure 6d replaces RECON accuracies of 92.94%, 80.32% and 55.70% with 90.96%, 81.96% and 55.92% for MNIST, FashionMNIST and GEOM-QM9. These are updated results under revised settings/reporting, including changed image k. Figure 5c revises MNIST and GEOM-QM9 OOD AUCs from 0.92 to 0.91 and 0.80 to 0.82. Substantial new comparator and diagnostic results include EquiAdapt exceeding RECON on MNIST and SEGNN reaching 98.55% on GEOM-QM9.

T1.justification: New Appendix D.1 defines the stabilizer S_x and states that pose distributions are identifiable only modulo it. Appendix D.5 adds an O(N²d) complexity analysis for naive neighborhood search. Proposition 3.1, the Appendix B proofs and the Tukey-Fréchet mathematics in Appendix C are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion remove the claim of the first symmetry-discovery demonstrations in 3D and clarify the target as instance-level pose distributions. The abstract adds a claim of matching or outperforming other canonicalizations. The central normalization, OOD-detection and inference-only canonicalization contributions remain.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds substantive discussion of stabilizer-induced pose ambiguity, inter-class latent overlap as a failure condition, and why molecular identity can remain separable despite conformational variation. It proposes targeted mitigation strategies and explains neighborhood-size tradeoffs. Appendix F additionally interprets the large gap to SEGNN as a limitation of canonicalization in the molecular setting.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the promised code release and hidden repository placeholder with a concrete repository address. It adds comparator architectures, training configurations and hyperparameter-search tables, plus pseudo-label runtimes and per-sample centering overhead. Existing RECON architecture and hardware documentation is largely retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 substantially expands positioning through LieGG, LieGAN, LaLiGAN, Implicit-PDF, Alignist and test-time canonicalization methods including EquiAdapt. It explicitly distinguishes instance-level pose estimation from dataset-level group discovery and explains differences in supervision and downstream-model dependence. The bibliography also adds supporting work on representation learning and efficient neighbor search.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion receive localized rewrites, including terminology changes to pose distributions and right translation. Appendix D is reorganized and Appendix F.2 gains domain-specific subsections. The main section sequence and most method, proof and implementation prose remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 6d gains comparator rows and a supervision column. The neighborhood plot becomes a broader two-panel display, the hit-rate figure gains an image panel, and new confusion-matrix and neighbor-example figures are added. Four new tables present runtimes, classifier comparisons and hyperparameter searches. The existing pose-distribution visualization moves from v2 Figure 11 to v3 Figure 9.

improvement.justification: The added relevant comparators substantially address v2's limited evidence for downstream utility. Expanded failure analyses, computational measurements, uncertainty reporting and concrete code-access information also make the benefits and limitations more assessable. These gains outweigh weaknesses in the additions: Appendix F tunes baselines on test accuracy and incorrectly states that EquiAdapt lowers GEOM-QM9 accuracy, whereas Figure 6d reports 52.96% versus 52.40% without canonicalization. Uncertainty reporting also remains incompletely specified.
